name: Anabolic steroid stacks (looksmaxxing)

lead: A stack is a combination of several anabolic-androgenic steroids, sometimes with growth hormone or other agents. On looksmaxxing forums, users ask for stacks that build muscle, shoulders, neck and a masculine, lean look, and some claim effects on the jaw and face.

The chain is muscle: the steroids bind and activate the androgen receptor, the same target as testosterone, which drives muscle growth and male secondary sex characteristics, producing a bigger, more masculine physique. Medicine approves steroids for conditions like low testosterone and delayed puberty, and non-medical use for appearance is documented, with studies describing most users as men around age 25. Published studies of specific stacks for facial appearance were not found.

paras: Users combine compounds for different reputed effects, run them in planned blocks, and pair them with heavy training and diet. Visible muscle changes build over weeks to months.

Medical sources list unfavourable cholesterol changes, hypertension, heart changes, suppression of the body's own testosterone production, testicular atrophy, fertility impairment, liver damage with some oral forms, acne and hair loss. In adolescents, steroids can prematurely close growth plates and stunt adult height. They are Schedule III in the US and Class C in the UK.

angle.text: Steroid combinations activate the androgen receptor to build muscle mass, neck and shoulders for a bigger, more masculine physique. Muscle gain from anabolic steroids is well documented; claims about facial bone and jaw width have not been tested.

lead: Anabolic steroid stacks are combinations of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS), often taken with other hormones, that users on looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums discuss for building muscle and a more masculine appearance. Users pursue a chain in which androgen receptor activation increases muscle mass and reduces fat, producing broader shoulders, a fuller physique and a leaner look. AAS are drugs structurally related to testosterone that act by binding to and activating the androgen receptor.[1]

Medical uses of AAS include testosterone replacement in men with low testosterone, inducing male puberty, treating certain anaemias and wasting conditions, and masculinising hormone therapy.[1] Non-medical use for appearance is documented, with studies describing most users as men with a median age near 25 who use them for how they look.[1]

Documented adverse effects include cardiovascular changes, suppression of natural testosterone production, fertility impairment and, in adolescents, premature closure of growth plates.[1] AAS are controlled substances in the US, UK and Canada.[1] Recent clinical commentary in dermatology, facial plastic surgery and paediatrics journals discusses steroids and injectable peptides as part of the looksmaxxing trend among young men.[2][3]
infobox: Schedule III (US), Class C (UK), Schedule IV (Canada)[1]

paras: A stack combines more than one compound. In forum threads, members propose combinations of testosterone esters and other androgens, sometimes adding growth hormone, thyroid hormone or selective androgen receptor modulators, to pursue goals such as wider shoulders, a stronger jaw and limited water retention. This article does not describe doses or protocols.

Approved or established uses include testosterone replacement in men with low testosterone, inducing male puberty, treating anaemias linked to leukaemia or kidney failure, supporting weight in chronic wasting, aiding recovery from burns and surgery, and masculinising therapy for transgender men.[1]

In looksmaxxing forums the aim is typically a more muscular or masculine look. One teenager asks which stack would avoid infertility and permanent hormone problems, while another thread proposes a stack for 'pubertymaxxing' with goals including broad clavicles and a masculine face.

Cardiovascular effects described include higher LDL and lower HDL cholesterol, hypertension, left ventricular thickening, arrhythmias, heart attack, stroke and sudden cardiac death, although the link to some heart changes is disputed.[1]

Long-term use suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, reducing natural testosterone production and causing testicular atrophy. Gynaecomastia can occur with aromatisable steroids, sperm production can be impaired, and infertility is usually reversible. Liver damage is associated mainly with oral 17-alpha-alkylated steroids, and acne and hair loss are also reported.[1]
In adolescents, AAS can accelerate bone maturation and prematurely close growth plates, stunting adult height.[1]

A sociological analysis of 8,072 comments from a large looksmaxxing forum described a community that encourages men to substantially alter their bodies and critiques physique and facial features through a masculine ideal.[4] A 2026 Missouri Medicine review lists the veterinary steroid trenbolone among the unregulated compounds promoted to young people through social media for cosmetic and athletic enhancement, and raises concerns about product contamination, inaccurate dosing and cardiovascular stress.[5]

Forum members also describe steroid use in bodybuilding spaces. On T Nation, a thread about two years of trenbolone use includes replies citing the deaths of several bodybuilders from heart disease and cardiac arrest, while other threads include users who say they run high doses with manageable side effects.[6][7] A separate T Nation thread argues that cycling steroids is not merely renting muscle gains, reflecting a long-running debate among users about whether size is retained after stopping.[8]

AAS are Schedule III controlled substances in the United States, Class C in the United Kingdom and Schedule IV in Canada, and controlled in many other countries. Where controlled, a black market supplies smuggled, clandestinely made or counterfeit products.[1] Most sporting bodies ban their use.[1]

No studies found on steroid stacks for facial or looksmaxxing outcomes. Clinical research on individual anabolic steroids concerns medical indications such as hypogonadism, and the safety literature on non-medical use is summarised in encyclopedic sources.[1]

Published commentary rather than trials documents the trend: a 2026 paediatrics article titled From Mewing to Peptides describes looksmaxxing as an emerging concern in young people, and a 2026 facial plastic surgery article discusses the boundary between self-enhancement and self-harm.[2][3]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, stack threads are common, often from younger members who say they are unsatisfied with gym progress or want puberty-stage facial and shoulder changes.

claims.claim: A well-designed stack can improve facial masculinity and skeletal width during or after puberty.
Stacks can be chosen to avoid infertility and hormone shutdown.
Adding growth hormone, thyroid hormone, insulin or SARMs to a stack improves the result.
Stacking several compounds lets users avoid the side effects of a single drug.
